text.p: Packaging, wine and appliances group Southcorp Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday that its wine unit grew strongly in the first half of 1996/97, but its appliance division grew strongest despite lower sales.

Southcorp chief executive office Graham Kraehe said the group's wine, packaging and appliance operations all increased pre-tax and interest earnings. Southcorp Wines' sales rose 14.6 percent to A$280.08 million, with a 27.5 percent rise in international sales, while earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) rose 14.3 percent to A$54.45 milllion, he said.
Southcorp Packaging maintained EBIT at A$64.20 million and improved margins due to rigorous cost management in flat market conditions where sales fell 2.6 percent to A$558.31 million.
The acquisition of the North American plastic packaging business Bennett Industries in August 1996 had made a worthwhile contribution with profit above expectations, he said.

Kraehe said Southcorp Appliances, operating against declining retail sales, the continuing downturn in the housing market, and rising import competition, had increased EBIT to A$18.84 million, up 29.1 percent, on sales which were down 5.6 percent to A$458.98 million.

Earlier, Southcorp reported a 22.3 percent rise in group net profit to A$64.92 million for the first half year. Pre-abnormal net profit rose 16.6 percent to A$62.9 million. Southcorp set an unchanged interim dividend of 8.25 cents per share.
Kraehe said the strong appliance division result reflected cost cuts better productivity, supported by the launch of a range of new whitegoods products, he said.

"The half year saw a significant turnaround in the heating and cooling division, but the whitegoods division suffered continuing pressure on market shares across all product categories," he said, adding this was caused by heavy
discounting by competitors in response to Southcorp launches.
The United States water heater business continued to improve, with cuts in operating losses under the new management team which provided a solid base for future growth, he said.
"As a result of the work undertaken to date, there had been approximately a A$4 million improvement in trading perfromance compared to the previous corresponding period," he said.
Southcorp said earlier it expected its current profit growth trend to continue and that strong earnings growth could be maintained for the balance of the year ending June 30, 1997.
Southcorp shares were up one cent at A$4.57 at 2.10 p.m. (0310 GMT).
